example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, office rent to Riverside Properties, 24 monthly bills from January 2027, built on 29 October 2026. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

messages.text: We signed a new office lease. Can you set up the rent as a recurring bill?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you give me the data yourself?
Is it a recurring journal entry, bill, invoice or subscription? With which supplier or customer?
What is the amount of each bill, and in which currency?
What is the start date, and the end date or the number of bills?
On which day? Please say "the 1st" or "the last business day". "Monthly" is not enough.
Which account, and which tax code if tax applies?
Which holiday calendar? And when a date falls on a holiday, do I move it forward or backward?
Does the amount increase, and when does it stop or pause?
If the first or last month is a part month, do I pro-rate by days or follow the contract?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. A bill to Riverside Properties, $8,500 a month in US dollars. 24 months from 1 January 2027, due on the 1st. Rent Expense, no sales tax. Due on receipt. US federal holidays, move forward. 3% more each year at the lease anniversary. No part months.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot create, post or schedule anything.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I build a **recurring bill** for **Northbrook Trading**: office rent to **Riverside Properties**, **$8,500 a month** in US dollars, on the **1st**. That is **24 bills** from **1 January 2027**, moved **forward** on the **US federal holiday calendar**.
messages.after: The coding is **Rent Expense**, with a **3% increase** at each lease anniversary. I check it against your books. Nothing will be posted. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
rows: Riverside, $8,500 on the 1st, no end date
Four monthly charges keyed by hand
messages.summary: One batch of reads. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.after: From January, the old and new templates would both bill you. Is the new lease a renewal of the old one?

messages.text: Yes, it renews on 1 January. The old template's last bill is on 1 December.
Then a person ends the old template after its **Tuesday 1 December 2026** bill, before the new one goes in. Here are the 24 new bills. Seven fall on a weekend or a holiday, so they move forward:
messages.after: The other 17 bills fall on business days. No bill leaves its month.

messages.text: The 3% increase starts at the first anniversary, 1 January 2028. In 24 months, it applies once:
messages.after: Each memo says why. Bill 13 reads "lease yr 2, $8,500 + 3% at 1 Jan 2028 anniversary = $8,755". Your lease runs 24 months, so lease accounting may apply. Please ask your accountant how to code it.

messages.after: The $7,200 insurance belongs to the prepaid schedule. The loan interest changes each month, so it is not a candidate. Which charges do you want templates for?

messages.text: Not Metro Shred. We check the shred count each month. I will look at the others. Can you just set up the rent in QuickBooks for me?
No. I cannot create, post or schedule anything in your books. A person enters the template from this specification:
messages.after: Each month, I can read the ledger and check that the rent posted, at the right amount and account. Do you want the six sheets as an Excel file? And shall I save your settings?

messages.text: Done. Here is **Riverside Properties_RecurringSchedule_2026-10-29.xlsx**, with Northbrook Trading on every sheet. I saved the holiday calendar, the forward move, the list of recurring bills and your reason for Metro Shred. I never save a rate.
